archetype: A mono-red Goblin swarm with a storm half bolted on. deck-audit establishes no archetype, so the BASE targets apply and no override was used; strategic_frame.json calls it "Mono-red Goblin swarm with a storm half bolted to it". The measured engine agrees with the frame's ordering: the token component assembles 60.0% at mean turn 3.184, the Zada component 66.1% at mean turn 5.266, and the storm component 26.5% at mean turn 4.914. Swarm is the floor, storm is the ceiling.
verdict: This deck functions and it converts. Mana is at or over target on every mana axis, the turn-3 land drop lands 90% of the time, and five checker-passed stacks record what the board actually does — including a mana-positive Haze of Rage loop that needs no commander at all. What limits it is the shape of its interaction, not the amount. I read all 13 oracle texts on the audit's interaction axis: 11 can point at an opposing permanent, and nearly all of that is damage, which never touches an enchantment, a land or a graveyard. A search of all 79 entries for destroy / exile target / target permanent / gain control / counter / return target returns four cards, and only Chaos Warp answers an opposing enchantment or land — a named singleton, which the corpus prices at 10.1% by ten cards seen.

findings.note: My prior open finding is cured, and the replacement claim survives attack. I ran the stated search over data/cards.csv myself (legal_commander == legal, color_identity in {'', 'R'}, cmc <= 4, type_line not Stickers, oracle text containing 'target permanent' or 'target nonland permanent' together with destroy|exile|shuffle|return|sacrifice|gain control): it returns exactly 26 rows. The five reasons partition those 26 EXACTLY — 8 own/control + 2 colour/type + 10 further-mana + 3 schedule + 1 no-answer = 24 non-hits, plus Wild Magic Surge and Chaos Warp; set equality against my search result holds with no duplicate across buckets, no card named that the search misses, and no card in the search left unnamed. The unreproducible '20 hits' figure is gone. The timing argument is true of the two cards I raised: Lux Cannon reads '{T}: Put a charge counter on this artifact. {T}, Remove three charge counters: Destroy target permanent' (any permanent, no further mana, but three turns of charge-up before the fourth tap kills), and Culling Scales reads 'At the beginning of your upkeep, destroy target nonland permanent with the lowest mana value' (your upkeep, mandatory, lowest-mv only). Both are ruled out on timing and not reach, exactly as the entry now concedes. Star Athlete verifies too — its trigger needs an attack and 'Its controller may sacrifice it', so the opponent chooses. The three cards the earlier query missed are handled correctly: Fury Charm's only destroy mode is 'Destroy target artifact' (it reaches the search on the unrelated time-counter mode), Oblivion Stone needs {5} to sacrifice, and Star Athlete is above. Canoptek Tomb Sentinel is subtly right — its exile trigger fires only 'when this creature enters from a graveyard', so the removal genuinely costs Unearth {7}. I also ran a WIDER net for on-demand catch-alls the stated query could miss (broad 'destroy target X or Y' / 'any permanent' phrasings in mono-red or colourless at cmc <= 4): 77 candidates, and every one is type-restricted (artifact, land, creature, blue permanent, or Goblin Cratermaker's colourless-only clause). No catch-all hides outside the query, so the re-scoped superlative — the only catch-all castable ON DEMAND among the 26 that this deck does not already run — is true. One immaterial imprecision inside a correct bucket: HELIOS One's activation is '{3}, {T}, Pay X {E}, Sacrifice' rather than a literal {5}-{7}, though each energy costs its own {1},{T} so the effective cost lands in that band, and the card is sorcery-only and kills only a permanent of mana value exactly X — it is correctly excluded, on a cost description that is loose by a few mana.

The first announced correction verified. The reading now says 'artifact has three answers (Goblin Trashmaster, Vandalblast, Chaos Warp)' where it previously said two. All three genuinely answer an artifact: Goblin Trashmaster 'Sacrifice a Goblin: Destroy target artifact', Vandalblast 'Destroy target artifact you don't control', Chaos Warp any permanent. The correction is internally consistent with the rest of the reading, which states that the measured 2 is a floor because the heuristic reads only cards carrying a removal role and therefore never sees Chaos Warp (confirmed: card_roles.json gives Chaos Warp no role at all, and _interaction_breadth's baseline artifact list is exactly ['Goblin Trashmaster','Vandalblast']). The load-bearing prescription is untouched — it rests on enchantment, land and graveyard, and the correction moves a number in the direction UNFAVOURABLE to the doctor's own case. The '10.1% by ten cards seen' figure is verbatim from strategy:deckbuilding.redundancy-vs-tutors and is the correct singleton row for a one-card class.

The second announced correction verified against card_roles.json directly. Every one of the four cards now carries its actual role: Grapeshot ['removal:damage'], Empty the Warrens ['threat:tokens'] (the correction — it was previously lumped into the removal/buff phrasing), Haze of Rage ['buff:pump'], Spreading Insurrection genuinely absent from the roles map. The load-bearing claim is unchanged and true: none of the four carries a wincon:* role. I enumerated wincon:* across the whole 99 and it returns exactly ['Goblin Dark-Dwellers', "Witch's Mark"], which is both the named pair and the measured value of 2, so the floor argument stands. The three cited stacks are all checker.verdict == pass.
